title: Chef John's Chinese Scallion Pancakes

Transfer dough onto a lightly floured work surface. Knead dough until sticky but relatively smooth and elastic, dusting with a minimal amount of flour if needed. Use a rolling pin to flatten dough into a rectangular shape about 1/8-inch thick, flipping over and dusting lightly with flour halfway through. | 6. Paint surface of the dough with the oil mixture until just covered, leaving 1 inch of space on the edges. Sprinkle scallions on top. Coil 1 end of the dough inward toward the middle; wrap the opposite end around the coil to finish, tucking the tip under the bottom. Heat vegetable oil in a cast iron skillet over high heat. Add 1 pancake; lower heat to medium. Cook until crispy and browned, about 4 minutes per side. Repeat with the other pancake. title: Chinese Steamed Buns

Transfer to a greased bowl, roll to coat with oil, and let sit until tripled in size, 2 ½ to 3 hours. | 6. Punch down dough and spread out on a floured board. Cover all 24 dough balls and let sit until doubled in size, about 30 minutes. | 9. Bring some water to a boil in a wok, then reduce heat to medium and keep water at a low boil. Place the steam plate on a small wire rack in the middle of the wok, leaving at least 2 inches of space between the plate and the wok. Working in batches, place buns on waxed paper squares onto the steam plate, leaving 1 to 2 inches between buns. | 10. Cover and steam buns for 15 minutes. Carefully remove the lid, so condensation doesn't drip onto buns. Continue steaming remaining buns until all are cooked.

title: Velveting Chicken Breast, Chinese Restaurant Style

title: Quick Beef Stir-Fry

title: Easy Chinese Fried Noodles

Heat remaining 1 teaspoon vegetable oil in the same wok or skillet over medium heat. Combine 2 tablespoons sesame oil with remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in the same skillet or a wok over medium heat. Stir in cooked vegetables, tossing frequently, until heated through, about 5 more minutes. | 9. Enjoy!

title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)

directions: 2. Gather all ingredients. | 3. Stir soy sauce, honey, ketchup, brown sugar, rice wine, hoisin sauce, red bean curd, and five-spice powder together in a saucepan over medium-low heat. title: Perfect Pot Stickers
ingredients: 1 pound ground pork | 4 cloves minced garlic | 0.5 cup finely chopped green onions | 3 tablespoons very finely minced fresh ginger | 2 tablespoons soy sauce | 1 teaspoon soy sauce | 1 teaspoon sesame oil | 1 pinch cayenne pepper | 1.5 cups finely chopped green cabbage | 2.5 cups all-purpose flour, or more as needed | 0.75 teaspoon kosher salt | 1 cup hot water, about 130 -150 F (55-65 C) | 0.25 cup seasoned rice vinegar | 0.25 cup soy sauce | 6 tablespoons vegetable oil for frying, or as needed - divided | 8 tablespoons water for steaming, divided

To make the dough: Place 2 ½ cups of flour and kosher salt in a mixing bowl. Slowly pour in hot water. Stir with a wooden spoon until mixture forms a shaggy dough. When dough has rested, divide into 4 equal pieces. Cover 3 pieces with a dish cloth while you work the first piece. Roll into a small log about the thickness of a thumb, about 3/4 inch. Lightly moisten the edges of a wrapper with your wet finger. Place a small scoop of the ground pork mixture onto the center of a wrapper. Fold up the 2 sides and pinch together in the center. title: General Tso's Chicken

title: Moo Shu Pork

title: Mongolian Beef and Spring Onions

title: Authentic Chinese Egg Rolls (from a Chinese person)
